look_here_first: Dark-stemmed woody mimosa with strongly curved downward prickles, few pairs of pinnae, pale pink flower heads, and short red-brown pods.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local + Personal List + 2 wild iNaturalist observations; UT PRC documents native NW Hays populations; ITIS/WFO accept species.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Fabaceae/Mimosa: bipinnate leaves, pulvini that can drive touch-sensitive movement in several species, globose heads of many tiny flowers, and segmented/prickly legumes. Habit, prickle placement, pinna count, and pod structure are especially useful.
best_field_traits: no more than about 7 leaflet pairs on longest pinnae
shorter red-brown pods, mostly sessile at base
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with M. borealis, texana is darker, more zigzag, and more strongly hooked. Compared with M. biuncifera, it has fewer pinnae/leaflets and less strongly constricted pods.
